text:
laura: Quick idea — can we add an optional "smoothing" window in the edge proxy to dampen short high-rate spikes from individual tenants before they hit admission? seems like a lightweight way to keep tail latency low for normal users while preventing tiny bursty abuse patterns.

mike: Do you mean per-tenant leaky-bucket at the proxy layer or a sliding-window avg?

laura: per-tenant leaky-bucket-ish. small local token bucket with short refill (200ms) and a soft-drop when over. not authoritative — still consult central quota for serious limits.

raj: i'd worry about split-brain semantics — proxy cache vs central quota could disagree during failover. what's the expected correctness model?

laura: good call. model is: proxy smoothing is best-effort latency control, not enforcement. central admission is still source-of-truth for capacity and long-term fairness. proxy should only delay or soft-drop (<5% of requests) and include provenance header for telemetry.

nina: how would this interact with priority tenants? we don't want smoothing to undo reserved capacity behavior for high-priority customers.

laura: config override: any tenant with reserved capacity or explicit bypass flag skips smoothing. default smoothing only applies to non-reserved, scored requests.

zane: can we see a mock config?

laura: here's a tiny example config we sketched:

```
proxy.smoothing.enabled: true
proxy.smoothing.window_ms: 200
proxy.smoothing.capacity: 8  # tokens
proxy.smoothing.soft_drop_pct: 5
proxy.smoothing.bypass_tags: ["reserved", "trusted"]
```

raj: telemetry needs to indicate when proxy soft-drops happen and the tenant score at the time. otherwise ops will chase ghosts. add headers like X-RDWD-Prox-Smooth and probe metrics: prox_smooth.count, prox_smooth.drop_count, prox_smooth.latency_ms.

mike: rollout plan idea: start with synthetic canaries + 1% of real traffic to a controlled proxy fleet, compare 95/99 latencies and token cost. also run abuse-sim tests to ensure it doesn't open new evasion vectors.

nina: abuse concern: attackers might craft low-cost calls that get smoothed then retried to bypass central admission spikes. need an indicator in central admission to treat prox-smoothed requests as higher-risk for scoring.

laura: agreed — propose adding prox_smooth flag to incoming requests so the central abuse detector raises score slightly for retried sequences. central should also continue to count tokens.

zane: any perf hit on proxy? local counters + small timers should be cheap, but we should measure. keep it opt-in per fleet.

op-sre-bot: deploy queued: smoothing-proxy-feature -> canary cluster (canary-3) at 2026-03-20T15:02:12Z :construction:

laura: next steps: write RFC short PR outlining accuracy model, config knobs, telemetry, and rollout test plan. volunteer to own the RFC. anyone want to pair on the abuse test harness?

raj: I can pair on the harness. can we include a test for combined short-burst + KV-cache-miss scenario (that amplifies cost)?

mike: i'll add the canary perf metrics dashboard tiles and a budget for synthetic load.

nina: i'll draft the abuse-detector tweak (prox_smooth signal) and link it in the RFC.

laura: awesome — i'll open the RFC later today and ping you all. :thumbsup:
